title: At 91, Dale Sanders Reclaims Appalachian Trail Age Record
summary:
Dale Sanders of Memphis, Tennessee, became the oldest person to hike the entire Appalachian Trail on August 31, 2026. At 91, he completed the 2,198-mile route in 359 days, reclaiming a record he had first set nine years earlier.

The Appalachian Trail runs from Springer Mountain in Georgia to Mount Katahdin in Maine. Its route includes forests, mountains and rocky terrain. According to the report, an official completion requires hikers to cover the entire trail within 365 days, but they do not have to make one continuous trip. Sections may be completed in different orders, with breaks between them.

That flexibility shaped Sanders' journey. He started on September 6, 2025, in Harpers Ferry, West Virginia, near the trail's midpoint. He chose his route so he could see Georgia's autumn leaves. During winter, he paused to avoid hiking in snow. He returned in spring and continued north toward Maine.

Sanders averaged about 12 miles a day, with one rest day each week. Even with those breaks, the journey tested his endurance. Only about a third of the more than 3,000 people who attempt the trail each year finish it, according to the report.

After a fall in Vermont, Sanders later experienced numbness in his left arm and went to a hospital in Maine. Tests identified a pinched nerve. He was eventually allowed to resume hiking. Exhausted and considering stopping, he received encouragement from family and supporters with 140 miles left.

Sanders first became the trail's oldest finisher in 2017, when he was 82. His friend M.J. Eberhart completed it at 83 in 2021, breaking that record with Sanders' encouragement. Watching his friend succeed helped prompt Sanders to seek the record again.

His other achievements include paddling the full Mississippi River at 80 and again at 87, and completing a 42-mile Grand Canyon hike at 85. Sanders credits daily exercise and a positive attitude for his ability to keep tackling long-distance challenges.
